answer: Relic-Seeded Challenge Lattice: each identity must submit a freshly generated, never-before-seen puzzle solution derived from a random seed bound to a unique physical relic (a hardware token’s marble-veined fingerprint), where the seed expires after one use. The enforcement rule: solutions are checked against a public velvet ledger of all prior seeds, and any repeated or precomputed solution is rejected. Attacker cost: must obtain and physically scan a new relic per identity, plus compute a unique solution within the short window—making mass sybil creation costly in hardware and time.
